To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
temporary workers in Australia are paid differently from their permanent counterparts.
the wage gap between temporary and permanent workers is not constant, but varies with the level of wages.

(i) the wage gap between workers with temporary and permanent employment contracts is large at the bottom of the wage distribution, but it is not large at the top of the wage distribution; and (ii) casual workers are more likely to have low-paid jobs and agency workers are more likely high-paid jobs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how temporary employment affects the wage distribution.
the structure of the wage differential between permanent workers and temporary workers.
the wage structure of temporary workers, and how it varies with permanent workers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
casual workers experience a large and persistent wage penalty, while temporary agency workers are usually well paid, and temporary contract workers receive a wage penalty only for the lowest paid.
temporary employment is associated with a wage penalty for low-paid workers and a wage premium for the most highly paid.
temporary workers are usually paid less than permanent workers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wage penalty for low-paid casual workers is not a universal feature of temporary jobs, and that the wage premium for agency workers is not a feature of low-wage temporary jobs.

there are large wage differentials for some groups of temporary workers, but that these differences are concentrated at the tails of the wage distribution and are therefore not a large concern for most workers.
temporary workers are paid less than permanent workers, but that there are important differences across the wage distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one-size-fits-all story about the wage gap for temporary workers.

there is a substantial variation in the wage differential between temporary workers and permanent workers, and that it is necessary to consider the whole wage distribution when examining wage differentials for temporary workers.
there are important differences in the structure of the wage gap for temporary workers.
